claim: Exploring the model's behaviour (sensitivity analysis) and comparing it with another model is standard when the real system cannot be observed
quote: Thus if a system is not observable, which is  often the case, it is usually not possible to obtain a ... high degree of confidence in the model. In this situ ation the model output behavi or(s) should be explored as thoroughly as possible and comparisons made to other valid models whenever possible.
locator: Sec. 8, pp. 189-190 printed (PDF pp. 7-8); Table 1 'Operational Validity Classification', p. 190
issue: Sargent prescribes exploring model behaviour (incl. parameter variability-sensitivity analysis) and comparison with 'other valid models'. The baseline attacker is not a validated model of an APT, so the comparison meets Sargent's form but not his condition; 'as is standard' also hardens his 'should ... whenever possible'. The sentence's own limit ('cannot take the findings beyond the simulation') matches Sargent's 'usually not possible to obtain a high degree of confidence'.
fix_text: 'and compared it with the baseline attacker, as is standard when the real system cannot be observed' -> 'as is recommended when the real system cannot be observed [sargent2011], and compared it with the baseline attacker'
